# Behavioral Specification: ADC Controller Interrupt Handling

## 1. Overview

This module collects interrupt events from the ADC controller, qualified them with per-source enable bits, and drives the associated interrupt state and interrupt request behavior.

The module supports the following interrupt event sources:

- Eight filter-match sources, corresponding to the eight ADC filters.
- One one-shot conversion-complete source.

For each source, the module receives an enable indication and an event indication. When a source is enabled and an event occurs, the module must:

- Set the corresponding sticky per-source event status bit.
- Cause the single interrupt state bit to be set.
- Assert the interrupt request output if the global interrupt enable is set.

If a source is not enabled, its events must not cause any of the above effects.

---

## 2. Reset Behavior

On reset of the event-capture logic:

- All pending filter-match information must be cleared.
- No captured event may be delivered after reset deassertion.

On reset of the interrupt-logic logic:

- The interrupt state must be cleared.
- The interrupt request output must be deasserted.
- No status-setting or interrupt-state-setting output may be produced while reset is asserted.

---

## 3. Filter-Match Event Handling

Filter-match events may arrive in a different clock domain from the main interrupt logic. The module must handle this safely without losing event information.

The module must:

- Capture each filter-match event when it arrives.
- Preserve the identity of each filter that matched.
- Hold pending filter-match events until they can be presented to the main-clock interrupt logic.
- Not drop a filter-match event that arrives while an earlier filter-match event is still pending.
- Present concurrently pending filter-match events together while preserving which filter sources matched.

When a filter-match event is presented:

- If the corresponding per-source enable bit is set, the module must set the sticky status bit for that filter source.
- Multiple filter sources may be set in the same cycle if multiple filters matched and were enabled.
- If a filter source is not enabled, that source must not cause a status bit update or interrupt-state update.

---

## 4. One-Shot Complete Event Handling

A one-shot conversion-complete event is an additional interrupt source.

When the one-shot complete event occurs:

- If its per-source enable bit is set, the module must set the sticky one-shot status bit.
- It must also cause the single interrupt state bit to be set.
- If the source is not enabled, the event must be ignored for interrupt generation.

---

## 5. Per-Source Event Status Behavior

The per-source status bits are sticky from the perspective of this module.

The module must:

- Set a per-source status bit when a qualified event for that source occurs.
- Never automatically clear a per-source status bit.
- Not clear a per-source status bit when a new event occurs.
- Not allow an already-set status bit to prevent a new event from being reported through the interrupt state logic.

---

## 6. Interrupt State and Interrupt Request Output

The module maintains a single interrupt state bit for all interrupt sources combined.

A qualified event on any source must set this interrupt state bit.

The interrupt request output must be asserted when:

- The interrupt state bit is set.
- The global interrupt enable bit is set.

The interrupt request output must be deasserted when:

- The global interrupt enable bit is cleared, or
- The interrupt state bit is cleared by software.

The interrupt request output must remain asserted, once asserted, until software clears the interrupt state or the global enable is cleared.

---

## 7. Interrupt Test Operation

The module must provide a software-accessible interrupt test mechanism.

When software writes a 1 to the interrupt test bit:

- The interrupt request output must be asserted.
- This assertion must not require a real event.
- This assertion must not require the global interrupt enable bit to be set.
- This assertion must not require any per-source enable bit to be set.

The test mechanism must allow the interrupt path to be exercised independently of event status.

---

## 8. Summary of Functional Requirements

The module must:

1. Accept eight filter-match event sources and one one-shot completion event source.
2. Preserve filter-match event information when crossing clock domains.
3. Qualify each event with its per-source enable bit.
4. Set the appropriate sticky per-source status bit only for qualified events.
5. Set the single interrupt state bit for qualified events.
6. Assert the interrupt request output when the interrupt state is set and the global interrupt enable is set.
7. Assert the interrupt request output when the interrupt test bit is written, regardless of enable or state.
8. Never clear per-source status bits automatically.
9. Initialize all event capture and interrupt state on reset.
